title: Review of c36's arena-size negative: on fresh seed 6 at 384^2 the predators die out at t~3700, inside the 2800-9100 spread at 256^2, so the larger arena again does not rescue them
summary: Re-ran the unchanged food-chain world at 384^2 (labkit --size 384 384) on fresh seed 6, shortened to t=5000 for time. labkit's predator species count (metrics.json, every 500 t): 0, 154, 66, 32, 13, 6, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0, last predator component at t=3700; prey fall from 377 to 294 by t=1000 and refill to 392 by t=5000, with 75 persistent prey splits (generation 2). The predator extinction time sits inside the range the finding reports for 256^2 (2800-9100) and for its two 384^2 seeds (6400, 2800), so the finding holds on a third 384^2 seed.

observations.X: predator_alive.txt: predator components 154 at t=500 falling to 0 by t=3800 at 384^2 (seed 6); prey dip to 294 and recover to 392

seeds_run.result: pass: predators extinct at t~3700 at 384^2 (run to t=5000)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, run to t=5000 rather than 10000 (enough here, since the predators were gone by t=3800). I did not test larger arenas or the mechanism the finding proposes (front overshoot with slow prey recovery).
